referents.why: first person singular ('from me') inside Pharaoh's speech, whose sender is cl1s; the speaker is Pharaoh
referents.category: first person inside a speech is its speaker

referents.why: first person singular possessive ('my people') inside Pharaoh's speech; the possessor is the speaker
referents.category: first person inside a speech is its speaker

referents.why: third masculine singular subject of 'he said' (wayyiqtol) right after cl0, whose subject is Pharaoh; the nearest agreeing referent that does the act of speaking
referents.category: narrative subject carried over from the preceding clause

referents.why: second masculine plural imperative 'pray' is addressed to the two men summoned in cl0; the composite Moses and Aaron agrees in number
referents.category: addressee of a command to several people

referents.why: subject of the jussive 'that he may remove the frogs' is the one asked in cl2 ('pray to the LORD'); third masculine singular; the LORD of cl2 is w12, while w31 is the LORD of cl5
referents.category: implied subject of an asked-for act

referents.why: first common singular 'I will let go' inside Pharaoh's speech; the speaker is Pharaoh
referents.category: first person inside a speech is its speaker

referents.why: third masculine plural 'that they may sacrifice' follows 'let go your people' (cl4); the people released are the nearest agreeing doer; w27 is 'your people', not w21 'my people', which are the ones the frogs leave
referents.category: third plural after a collective is released

links.why: reversed direction: the summoning (cl0) is the earlier event and the saying (cl1) follows it, so the sequence is cl0 then cl1, which is already kept
wayyiqtol 'and he said' continues the narrative after 'he summoned'
a waw joining a command (second person imperative) to a jussive in a different person is 'so that', not a plain 'and'
links.category: command joined to a change of person

links.why: the praying is for the removal of the frogs: command, then waw and a jussive in a different person (third)
links.category: command joined to a change of person

links.why: a jussive followed by a cohortative in a different person is a promise, which purpose excludes; the sense is conditional, but no marker or link type states it, so the plain waw stays
cohortative 'I will let go' then jussive 'that they may sacrifice' in a different person; the release is for the sacrifice, which is purpose
the release is for the sacrifice: a directive clause (force directive) then a jussive in a different person, the second being the aim of the first
cl1 is the saying clause; what is said is the imperative group imp2 (command cl2, with its aim cl3 and effect cl4)

groups.why: Pharaoh's speech to Moses and Aaron; sender was the slot cl1s, now its candidate w2; addressee added (the command's 'you' is c3); the command group is a part, and cl5 is the speech's own part; the builder listed the commands directly as parts
groups.category: speech with addressee and nested command

groups.why: one command ('pray') with its aim (the removal, cl3) and the promised effect (the release, cl4); the builder's part role is not an imperative member
cl3 is the aim of the command in imp2, not a command of its own; the jussive is a clause of the prayer
groups.category: jussive wrongly taken as a command

groups.why: cl4 is the effect of imp2 and cl5 is a part of the speech; cl4 is a promise, not a command, and no group kind names a promise
groups.category: promise wrongly taken as a command

none_fit.what: a promise made conditional on a request, with no conditional particle; the conditional group needs an 'if' clause and the if link needs a condition marker, so neither fits

cant_tell.what: whether the release in cl4 is conditional on the removal in cl3
cant_tell.why: the sense reads as conditional, but the form carries no marker and the plain waw is not decisive

cant_tell.what: whether the release in cl4 is the effect of the command group imp2 or a separate promise
cant_tell.why: the imperative kind says what a command brings about; the release is what Pharaoh promises if the frogs go, which fits effect only loosely and no kind names a promise
